paths.naming: Controller settings use flat `key value` lines: <system>.input.port<n>.<device>.<button>, device selectors gamepad|dualanalog|none, and native `joystick 0x<128-bit id> button_<n>` / `abs_<n>[-+][ scale]` expressions
paths.path: ~/.mednafen/mednafen.cfg (base directory is $MEDNAFEN_HOME if set, else $HOME/.mednafen); module overrides <base>/<system>.cfg and per-game <base>/<filesys.path_pgconfig, default pgconfig>/<FileBase>.<system>.cfg; settings are flat 'key value' lines with ';'#' comments and a legacy ';VERSION 0.' header format rejected by lunchbox. Controller bindings live in the same cfg layers as <system>.input.port<n>.<device>.<button> keys, e.g. gb.input.port1.gamepad.a or psx.input.port2.dualanalog.circle; device selection via <system>.input.port<n> (gamepad|dualanalog|none), multitaps via psx.input.pport<n>.multitap and ss.input.sport<n>.multitap, global input.joystick.axis_threshold (default 75); values are native expressions 'joystick 0x<128-bit id> button_<n>' / 'abs_<n>[-+][ scale]'; any setting can also be overridden on the command line as -<setting> <value> (main.cpp usage example: -pce.stretch aspect)
evidence: docs:mednafen.github.io/documentation (mednafen.cfg under base directory; written at shutdown)

paths.path: <base>/sav/ (filesys.path_sav, default 'sav' under the base directory, not beside the ROM); backups in <base>/b/
paths.naming: saveram naming = ROM basename (FileBase) + per-system extension via filesys.fname_sav default %f.%M%x: PSX <base>.<slot>.mcr (e.g. gamename.0.mcr), GB <base>.sav, NES <base>.sav (FDS <base>.fds), SNES <base>.srm (+ .rtc), Saturn <base>.bkr, NGP <base>.flash, Virtual Boy <base>.sav, GBA <base>.sav plus <base>.eep for EEPROM
evidence: source:psx.cpp '%d.mcr', gb.cpp 'sav', nes/cart.cpp 'sav', nes/fds.cpp 'fds', snes/interface.cpp 'srm'/'rtc', ss.cpp 'bkr', ngp/neopop.cpp 'flash', vb/vb.cpp 'sav', gba/GBA.cpp 'sav'/'eep' @ f0ee9d5

paths.path: <base>/mcs/ (filesys.path_state, default 'mcs' directory under the base directory)
paths.naming: filesys.fname_state default %f.%M%X: generic gzip-compressed save states named <base>.mc<slot> for slots 0-9 (the uniform 'mcs' extension with the slot digit replacing its last character); no per-ROM .nst and no per-system state extension - the .mcs/mc<N> scheme is shared by all emulation modules
evidence: source:general.cpp MDFN_MakeFName MDFNMKF_STATE (%x defaults to 'mcs', slot merged into X) + state.cpp MDFN_MakeFName(MDFNMKF_STATE, CurrentState, NULL) @ f0ee9d5

paths.naming: Firmware filenames are per-module settings: PSX scph5500.bin/scph5501.bin/scph5502.bin have documented SHA-256 values; other listed Saturn/PCE/GBA/FDS names have no checksum disposition in the pinned record
paths.path: <base>/firmware/ (filesys.path_firmware; BIOS setting values are resolved there unless absolute); per-system keys: psx.bios_jp/psx.bios_na/psx.bios_eu (defaults scph5500.bin/scph5501.bin/scph5502.bin with documented SHA-256), ss.bios_jp (sega_101.bin), ss.bios_na_eu (mpr-17933.bin) plus ss.bios_stv_* variants, pce.cdbios (syscard3.pce) and pce.gecdbios, pce_fast.cdbios, optional gba.bios (default empty), NES FDS disksys.rom

linux.notes: Lunchbox pins deep Mednafen contracts (docs/MEDNAFEN_STANDALONE_PROGRESS.md; controller_catalog mednafen-settings transport) and launches with a child-only MEDNAFEN_HOME private base, staged private config layers and bubblewrap mounts; only configuration files are replaced, native save/state locations are retained (controller_mednafen/native_command.rs, discovery.rs, isolation). Native 128-bit joystick IDs come from joydev/evdev inventory, never SDL GUIDs.

macos.notes: Verified via docs:mednafen.github.io/releases: macOS has no official binaries; releases ship Windows builds and source tarballs, with FreeBSD/Linux/NetBSD/OpenBSD/Windows listed as compiled platforms, so macOS runs only source builds (Homebrew formulae 'mednafen', MacPorts). Lunchbox's native Mednafen adapter (joydev/evdev inventory, bubblewrap isolation) is Linux-only.

linux-flatpak.reason: Mednafen's official release page provides Windows binaries and source/Unix build guidance but no trustworthy Flatpak package.
